title: FastBox Delivery Simulator
text: A deterministic delivery simulator that assigns packages to the nearest agent, follows delivery routes, and reports efficiency. Built for a Python developer assignment, FastBox separates input validation, package assignment, stateful simulation, and reporting. The runtime uses the Python standard library. Its README explains routing assumptions, ties, rounding, and agents with no deliveries. Accepts dictionary and list input schemas for warehouses and agents. Assigns packages using Euclidean distance, with deterministic agent-ID tie breaking. Simulates warehouse-to-destination movement in input order. Exports JSON efficiency reports and optional top-performer CSV output. Validates duplicate IDs, coordinates, warehouse references, and missing agents. Technologies: Python, JSON, CSV, unittest, GitHub Actions. Efficiency is average distance per package; lower is better. This is a deterministic simulator, not a live delivery service.

title: Designing a responsive voice pipeline
text: Why audio transport, context, retrieval, and response streaming belong in the same latency conversation. A voice interaction crosses several boundaries: incoming audio, transcription, reasoning, knowledge lookup, and spoken output. Improving one model call does not automatically improve the whole experience. A useful design makes each stage visible and measures the path from speech input to the first useful response. The professional voice-agent work described in this portfolio combines FastAPI, AsyncIO, WebSockets, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, and retrieval. Python’s AsyncIO is designed for concurrent code using async and await. It is a natural foundation for coordinating I/O such as incoming audio and outgoing response streams. A streaming pipeline also needs explicit handling of interruption, cancellation, and buffering. Those concerns are design considerations for a responsive system, rather than evidence that every implementation already handles them. The resume describes a dual-model architecture: a fast model supports immediate intent suggestions, while a higher-capacity model performs deeper retrieval over vector knowledge. Redis handles session state and cross-memory tracking. The separation allows different stages to serve different purposes. Context management still needs clear session boundaries so information belongs to the right conversation. The resume reports sub-800 ms voice interaction latency and 85%+ retrieval accuracy in call-center workflows. Those figures are reported outcomes, not a benchmark reproduced by this website. To evaluate a similar design, record stage timings, observe the slowest paths, and compare response usefulness as well as speed. The interactive latency explorer in the AI Lab is an illustrative way to inspect a sequential budget; real streaming stages can overlap.

title: Small Python tools, explicit decisions
text: How the FastBox simulator makes routing rules, tie breaking, and reporting assumptions inspectable. FastBox reads warehouse, agent, and package data, assigns each package to its nearest agent, simulates delivery routes, and writes an efficiency report. Its runtime uses only the Python standard library. That narrow scope makes the contract understandable: an input dataset and documented rules should produce a predictable report. The README explicitly addresses details that are easy to leave implicit. Assignment uses each agent’s original location. Equal distances resolve to the lexicographically smallest agent ID. Packages follow their original input order. An agent does not automatically return to a depot after the last delivery. These decisions make the result explainable and prevent a later refactor from quietly changing behavior. The loader validates duplicate identifiers and JSON keys, missing fields, coordinates, warehouse references, and packages without agents. Keeping normalization and validation separate from assignment and simulation makes each responsibility easier to inspect. The project structure reflects that separation through parser, models, assignment, simulation, and reporting modules. The report includes agents with zero deliveries. Their efficiency is null, and they are excluded from best-agent selection. Distances are calculated at full precision and rounded only for serialization. Average distance per delivered package is the efficiency measure, so lower is better. The README documents automated tests and a CI workflow; the portfolio does not claim to have executed that external project’s test suite.

title: From a local record to a useful interface
text: What the attendance and healthcare projects demonstrate about storage, relationships, and usable data. The attendance application provides a simple workflow: enter a name, mark attendance, and view records. A Tkinter interface handles the input while SQLite preserves records in a local file. A timestamp makes each event meaningful when it is read later. The reviewed source focuses on marking a person present, rather than a complete school-management system. The app creates an attendance table, inserts records through parameterized SQL, commits changes, and retrieves rows for display. SQLite is a file-based database that does not require a separate database server. Python’s official documentation recommends parameter placeholders for binding values. The repository uses that approach for names, timestamps, and status values. Smart Healthcare SQL models patients, doctors, and appointments. The appointment table links to patients and doctors using foreign keys. A reporting query joins the three tables to produce readable appointment information, while an aggregation calculates average waiting time per doctor. This moves the schema beyond a set of disconnected tables. These repositories are focused learning projects. Their source demonstrates storage and query concepts, but it does not establish production security, role management, medical use, or deployed reporting services. A descriptive portfolio is more useful when readers can see both the implemented behavior and the next engineering questions. Further work could explore migrations, pagination, richer validation, and tests around reporting behavior.
